key_insight: LIBERO-PeRM introduces a benchmark designed to measure whether robots can not only complete manipulation tasks, but also satisfy individual user preferences. It separates task success from personalization, making preference-following in embodied agents easier to study and compare.
problem_solved: Existing robotic manipulation benchmarks focus mainly on task completion and do not cleanly evaluate personalization. This paper addresses the lack of a controlled benchmark for personalized robotic manipulation, where the robot must adapt its behavior to user preferences in addition to accomplishing the task.
method: Introduces LIBERO-PeRM, a benchmark for personalized robotic manipulation and preference learning in embodied agents.
Defines evaluation settings that disentangle functional task performance from preference satisfaction.
Uses a structured set of questions to probe zero-shot preference following and other aspects of personalized robot behavior.
impact: This benchmark gives researchers a standard way to test whether robot policies can adapt to human preferences, not just execute commands. For practitioners, it enables clearer evaluation of personalization methods and supports development of robots that are more practical in household environments.
visual_elements: Benchmark pipeline showing task completion vs. preference satisfaction as separate tracks
Side-by-side robot behavior examples illustrating different user preferences
Evaluation matrix or table for the five benchmark questions
Icon set for household settings, preferences, and embodied agent interaction
paper_authors: Zhixu Li, Keqian Tang, Litian Gong, Jingyu Yao, Wenqian Zhang
